metadata.title: GDPR Standardized Regulatory Control Catalog
metadata.remarks: Generated by Automated Compliance Mapping Framework (Step 1: Ingestion & Standardization with Socio-Technical Friction Analysis).

props.name: ambiguity_triggers
props.value: appropriate; costs of implementation; nature, scope, context and purposes; organisational measures; regularly; state of the art; taking into account; timely

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: Taking into account the state of the art, the costs of implementation and the nature, scope, context and purposes of processing as well as the risk of varying likelihood and severity for the rights and freedoms of natural persons, the controller and the processor shall implement appropriate technical and organisational measures to ensure a level of security appropriate to the risk.

parts.name: item
parts.prose: Pseudonymisation and Encryption: The pseudonymisation and encryption of personal data.

parts.name: item
parts.prose: Confidentiality and Resilience: The ability to ensure the ongoing confidentiality, integrity, availability and resilience of processing systems and services.

parts.name: item
parts.prose: Incident Recovery and Restoration: The ability to restore the availability and access to personal data in a timely manner in the event of a physical or technical incident.

parts.name: item
parts.prose: Evaluation of Effectiveness: A process for regularly testing, assessing and evaluating the effectiveness of technical and organisational measures for ensuring the security of the processing.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose:
### Socio-Technical Friction Analysis (Rating: High)

**Automation Feasibility:** Non-Binary / Qualitative Governance Review Required

**Indeterminacy Rationale:** Mandates 'state of the art' protections without prescribing static cryptographic or architectural baselines. Hardcoding fixed parameters (e.g., TLS 1.3 or specific AES modes) into static Policy-as-Code creates rapid obsolescence and false assurance as cryptographic standards evolve. Contains subjective proportionality standards ('appropriate', 'proportionate', 'reasonable'). A binary boolean evaluation (Pass/Fail) cannot weigh the entity's size, operational risk profile, or threat environment against the technical burden of implementation. Requires balancing security controls against the 'costs of implementation' and the 'nature, scope, context and purposes of processing'. Economic feasibility and contextual business necessity are fundamentally socio-organizational judgments inaccessible to static code scanners. Relies on open-ended temporal thresholds ('without undue delay', 'timely', 'promptly'). While log event timestamps can measure elapsed time, determining whether a delay was 'undue' depends on forensic complexity and containment velocity. Enforces organizational, governance, or human factor safeguards (e.g., 'organisational measures', 'awareness', 'competent staff'). Cloud infrastructure assertions cannot ascertain human training retention, segregation of duties efficacy, or governance meeting integrity.

**Engineering Recommendation:** Establish an automated telemetry pipeline linked to NIST/ENISA vulnerability repositories to dynamically refresh baseline benchmarks. Implement a Tiered Control Matrix where automated CI/CD checks enforce minimal hygiene, while context-dependent risk waivers are reviewed by GRC leadership.

**Human-in-the-Loop (HITL) Validation Procedures:**

- Quarterly Cryptographic & Architecture Review by the Principal Security Architect.

- Documented Risk Acceptance & Proportionality Rationale signed off by the CISO/Data Protection Officer (DPO).

- Annual Cost-Benefit & Impact Assessment attesting to control proportionality.

- Post-Incident Triage Review validating incident timeline logs against operational complexity records.

- Human-in-the-Loop verification of training completion metrics and role-based access review attestations.

controls.title: Notification of a personal data breach to the supervisory authority

props.name: ambiguity_triggers
props.value: appropriate; undue delay; where feasible; without undue delay

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: In the case of a personal data breach, the controller shall without undue delay and, where feasible, not later than 72 hours after having become aware of it, notify the personal data breach to the supervisory authority competent in accordance with Article 55, unless the personal data breach is unlikely to result in a risk to the rights and freedoms of natural persons.

parts.name: item
parts.prose: Breach Description: Describe the nature of the personal data breach including where possible, the categories and approximate number of data subjects concerned and data records concerned.

parts.name: item
parts.prose: Contact Point: Communicate the name and contact details of the data protection officer or other contact point where more information can be obtained.

parts.name: item
parts.prose: Consequences: Describe the likely consequences of the personal data breach.

parts.name: item
parts.prose: Remediation Measures: Describe the measures taken or proposed to be taken by the controller to address the personal data breach, including, where appropriate, measures to mitigate its possible adverse effects.
